clue.text: Water falling, cloud in sight?

blocks.note: first meaning: a large, steep waterfall
second meaning: an eye condition that clouds the lens and blurs vision

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rain falling from a cloud you can see; the two halves are separate meanings, one a waterfall, the other the eye disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is both a big waterfall and an opacity of the eye's lens that clouds a person's vision.

clue.text: Mean hail storm

blocks.note: Ave is a Latin greeting, to hail someone
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A spiteful hailstorm battering the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective describing the storm, but it is the statistical noun, and 'hail' is a greeting rather than weather.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic average of a set of values.

clue.text: Musical in need of opening song

indicators.note: lacking its opening means the show's title loses its first letter

blocks.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A stage show that badly needs a good opening number.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, so it serves as a word for a song.

clue.text: Cupid got off lightly in the end, not knowing right from wrong

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: the state of not knowing right from wrong

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: Amor is the Latin name for Cupid, the god of love
alit is an old past tense of alight, to get off a vehicle
the last letter of lightly

explanation.surface: Cupid escaped with a light punishment because he couldn't tell right from wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorality is the absence of any moral sense, being unaware of or indifferent to right and wrong.

clue.text: Trunk warmer, result of sun on back of Buick Super

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a suntan is what the sun produces on skin
the final letter of Buick
super and top both mean excellent

explanation.surface: A car's boot heater, made from the sun beating on the rear of a Buick Super model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' is American for a car boot, matching the Buick, but here it is the human torso. A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless sweater worn over a shirt, warming the wearer's torso, or trunk.

clue.text: FBI suspect one of its agents hit

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy or not right, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
a Fed is an American slang term for an FBI agent

explanation.surface: The Bureau suspects one of its own agents has struck someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a verb with the FBI as its subject; it is an adjective signalling the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To biff is informal British for striking someone with a punch, so biffed is a past tense for hit.

clue.text: Implacable attorney lodges complaint

indicators.note: the phrase gives lodging to, or houses, the letters within it

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A relentless lawyer files a formal complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodges' looks like the legal sense of lodging a complaint; it actually says the phrase holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is a feeble, whining grumble, so it is an informal word for a complaint.

clue.text: That woman spreads thick toast for detective

indicators.note: she spreads herself between the words on either side, sitting in the middle

blocks.note: fat and thick both mean broad or plump
her refers to a woman
to toast bread is to brown it

explanation.surface: A woman generously buttering thick toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman sits between the thick and the toast, like filling. Father Brown is G K Chesterton's priest-sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Brown is the Catholic priest who solves crimes in G K Chesterton's stories, a classic fictional detective.

clue.text: Teary having plucked flanks, choose wax remover

indicators.note: plucking a word's flanks pulls off the letters at its two sides

blocks.note: taken as written
to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: A tearful person who has plucked hair from their sides picks a depilatory wax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wax remover' suggests hair waxing to go with the plucking; it is a tool for clearing earwax.
explanation.definitionFit: An earpick is a small implement for scooping wax out of the ear canal.

clue.text: Facilities costing extra, landlord leaving note

blocks.note: dear means expensive
the john is American slang for the toilet, the facilities
a landlord lets property, so is one who lets

explanation.surface: A landlord charges extra for amenities and then leaves a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' are the toilet, and the fragments run in the clue in reverse of their order in the answer. 'Leaving note' looks like the landlord leaving, but it is a note announcing someone's departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dear John letter is one ending a romantic relationship, the note a partner writes when walking out.

clue.text: Unlikely to run like Usain Bolt, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: of a dye, colourfast and not bleeding in the wash
second meaning: quick, as the Jamaican sprinter is

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the world's fastest sprinter would be unlikely to run; the first meaning is about dyes that do not bleed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast describes a dye fixed so it will not wash out, and also means quick, like the record-holding sprinter.

clue.text: One crater formed, and no more dinosaurs

definitions.note: the answer can be singular or plural; here it is the plural

indicators.note: something formed has been shaped into a new arrangement, so these letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
tops means at most, no more than

explanation.surface: An impact crater formed, and dinosaurs were wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to the asteroid strike that ended the dinosaurs; 'no more' is not extinction but the slang 'tops', as in ten pounds, tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Triceratops was a three-horned plant-eating dinosaur; the name serves as its own plural.

clue.text: The opposite article is on taxes

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
tithes are levies of a tenth, a church tax
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper item takes the contrary line on taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is on' places the word is after the taxes in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is the direct contrary of something, its exact reverse.

clue.text: Couple in the back of huge car could be stars

indicators.note: a couple from the back means the final pair of letters of the next word

blocks.note: the last two letters of huge
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A pair squeezed into the back seat of a big car might be celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like the twins of the answer, but it only takes two letters; the definition is 'stars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is a constellation, a named group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Military staff protects old president, cycling this?

definitions.text: Military staff protects old president, cycling this?
definitions.note: the whole clue is an extended definition: a bike you pedal

indicators.note: cycling a word rotates its letters, here moving the first one round to the end
the staff protects by wrapping around what it guards

blocks.note: a pike is a long spear carried by infantry
George Bush, a former US president

explanation.surface: An armed guard protecting an ex-president on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush cycled becomes USHB, which sits inside the pike. 'Cycling' does double duty: it turns the president round and hints at what you do on the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushbike is an ordinary pedal bicycle, the kind you go cycling on.

clue.text: Broke circumnavigators finally fixed boat and got on

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
fixed can mean rigged or rearranged, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of circumnavigators
taken as written
to get on is to grow old, so got on means aged

explanation.surface: Penniless round-the-world sailors repaired their vessel and set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like penniless, describing the sailors; it is the past tense of break, deliberately wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage something is to break or wreck it on purpose, so sabotaged means deliberately broke.

clue.text: Need less depth in J R Ewing's first novel

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away
in places the shortened word inside the letters that follow
first points to the opening letter of the surname

blocks.note: jay is how the letter J is spelt out
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for depth
taken as written
the first letter of Ewing

explanation.surface: A Dallas villain's first need is less depth.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare letter J must be written out as the word for it before anything can go inside. J R Ewing was the scheming oil baron in the US soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel about a governess, a classic of English fiction.

clue.text: In a bar take drugs, possibly hard

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a rod is a bar of metal or wood
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub taking drugs, maybe hard ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' looks like hard drugs, but it is the definition: sexual arousal. A rod is a bar, and USE goes inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aroused is sexually excited, and an aroused man may possibly be hard.

clue.text: Ten bats with red or white splice

indicators.note: bats means crazy or mad, so these letters go haywire

blocks.note: taken as written
red and white are the two common kinds of wine

explanation.surface: Ten cricket bats bound together with red or white tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like cricket bats, and 'splice' is the joint of a cricket bat's handle to its blade, but bats means crazy here.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is to join ropes or strands by weaving them together, which is to entwine them.

clue.text: Nearly all bed covers left under the table

indicators.note: nearly all of a word means all except its final letter
one word covers another by wrapping around it

blocks.note: a bed, as of a river, is its bottom
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Nearly all the bedclothes have been left under the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the table' looks like a place where bed covers lie; it is the idiom for so drunk you fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, the state of someone drunk enough to end up under the table.

clue.text: Defeat, on splits in armistice

indicators.note: the word splits and goes in separately, each part placed within the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
an armistice is a truce

explanation.surface: Losing a war, one side violates the ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of on go into the truce separately, one after TR and one after U.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to defeat them heavily and decisively.

clue.text: The French enjoy the smell they make and down their wee

blocks.note: BO is body odour, the smell people make
nap is the soft, downy surface of fabric
petit is French for small, which is wee in Scottish usage

explanation.surface: A rude jibe that the French relish their own smells and drink their urine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers back to the French, so their word for wee is petit. 'Wee' wants to be urine, but it is small.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon appétit is the French wish to diners to enjoy their meal, literally good appetite.

clue.text: Spike attached to stone overhangs

blocks.note: the stone of a fruit is its pit
on can mean fixed to, as in a coat on a hook
a placement word only: in a down entry the stone hangs over the other piece, so it comes first

explanation.surface: A climbing spike fixed to a rock overhang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhangs' is a placement signal in a down clue: the stone sits above the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike driven into rock to support a climber's rope.

clue.text: Corner immediately after turning right

indicators.note: turning round means the letters face the other way

blocks.note: on can mean straight after, as in on arrival
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: Instructions to turn right just past a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or sheltered corner of a room.

clue.text: Fine doctor cuts man loose after adapting carpenter's tool

indicators.note: adapting means altering, so these letters are changed into a new order
something that cuts into a word lands inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
fine and thin both mean slender
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A good doctor frees a man after an operation using a woodworking tool.
explanation.walkthrough: THIN and GP go together into the middle of the rearranged man loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothing plane is a short hand plane a carpenter uses to give wood a final smooth finish.

clue.text: Grazing the top half of foliage

indicators.note: the top half of a down entry means its first half, so the second half is dropped

blocks.note: the leaves of a plant are its foliage

explanation.surface: Animals grazing on the upper half of a tree's foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grazing' looks like a verb for animals eating, but it is a noun for grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or pasture, land given over to grazing for livestock.

clue.text: Expected Tertius or Quintus, possibly but not Sextus

definitions.text: Tertius or Quintus, possibly but not Sextus

blocks.note: first meaning: very likely to happen, as a betting favourite

blocks.clueFragment: Tertius or Quintus, possibly but not Sextus
blocks.note: second meaning: Roman names meaning third and fifth child describe an odd-numbered boy, while sixth is even

explanation.walkthrough: Tertius, Quintus and Sextus were Roman forenames for the third, fifth and sixth child; three and five are odd, six is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a likely winner in betting, hence expected; read as two words it is a third or fifth male child.

clue.text: Nurse rapped for messing up last sheet

indicators.note: messing up a word scrambles it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse is scolded for making a mess of the final bed sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheet' suggests bedding to go with the nurse; it is a page of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the blank leaf at the very end, or start, of a book, glued to the cover.
